run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Make `Field.Control` sync controlled value changes into field state (dirty, filled, validity, form errors) through `useValueChanged` like the sibling controls, register the serialized value so non-string dirty baselines compare correctly, honor `details.cancel()`, and, per the description, stop latching `data-focused` when a focused control unmounts or becomes disabled.
summary.issue_fit: No issue exists; alignment was judged against the caller-supplied pull-request title and body (mui/base-ui#5460, merged). Seven of eight description promises are met in code and covered by the new tests. The promised `data-focused` unlatch on unmount/disable is absent from the diff and the head file. Two description statements do not match the code: the `processedValueRef` guard does not exist (controlled `onChange` returns early instead), and the body says `clearErrors(name)` is not called while the head calls it on every controlled value change.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed in full against the merge-base, with FieldRoot, useFieldValidation, useFieldControlRegistration, useRegisterFieldControl, Form, FormContext, FieldValidity, useValueChanged, and the sibling controls read for callers and conventions. Reviewer ran the changed test file and the field/form/input/fieldset jsdom group at the head: all passed. One untracked file (`.mcp.json`) in the clone is outside the committed range and not reviewed. Chromium-only tests, typecheck, and lint were not run offline.

ambiguities.applied: Treated as a requirement gap of the change: the description is the sole intent source for this target, and the rubric makes an omitted acceptance requirement this change's responsibility even in unchanged code. The remedy explicitly allows dropping the claim instead of implementing it.
readings: The description promised the fix, so the merge owes either the implementation or a corrected description (applied).

findings.title: Deliver or drop the promised data-focused unlatch
findings.trigger: The description says a control that unmounts or becomes disabled while focused no longer latches `data-focused`, but the diff adds no such code: at head `setFocused(false)` is still reached only from `onBlur`, the relocated `autoFocus` effect has no cleanup, and `FieldRoot` never resets `focused` on `disabled`.
findings.impact: When a focused control is conditionally unmounted or disabled, no blur fires, so `Field.Root`, `Field.Label`, and `Field.Description` keep `data-focused` and focused styling, the bug the description claims is fixed.
findings.change: Either clear the focused state in `FieldControl.tsx` with a layout-effect cleanup on unmount and when `disabled` turns true while the control is the active element, adding a test for each path, or remove the claim from the description.
findings.source: pr-body/"A control that unmounts or becomes disabled while focused no longer latches `data-focused`, since no blur fires in that path."

questions.title: Is the Field.Validity value type change for non-string controlled values an accepted break?
questions.evidence: The control now registers `String(value)` (`FieldControl.tsx:86-97`), so `Field.Validity`'s public render-prop state, which spreads `validityData` (`FieldValidity.tsx:29-35`), reports `initialValue` as `"5"` instead of `5` on mount for `<Field.Control value={5}>`, and `value` as `"5"` after submit-time or imperative validation; the `validate` callback receives the same string on those paths. Both fields are typed `unknown` in the docs, `value` was already the DOM string after any keystroke at the merge-base, `onFormSubmit` values are unchanged, and no in-repo consumer reads these fields for a non-string control. The description does not mention the externally visible type change and the changelog marks breaking changes explicitly.
questions.why_it_matters: If maintainers treat the type of these public fields as part of the released contract, the change needs a breaking-change note or a raw-value baseline kept alongside the serialized comparison; if not, nothing further is owed. Status is already Changes Requested, so the answer affects release notes rather than this merge decision.
questions.answer: A Base UI maintainer decides whether `Field.Validity.State.value`/`initialValue` and the submit-time `validate` argument for non-string controlled `Field.Control` values are contractually raw; yes reopens this id as a compatibility finding, no closes it.

observations.fact: The description's `processedValueRef` guard is not in the code; the head returns early from `onChange` for controlled inputs and routes every controlled update through `useValueChanged(serializedValue, ...)`, which the new once-per-keystroke validation test covers.
observations.evidence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:105-115`, `:142-146`; `FieldControl.test.tsx` "validates once when a controlled value is changed by the user".

observations.fact: The description says this PR does not call `clearErrors(name)` on value changes, but the head calls it on every controlled value change, so the body's open question is already resolved toward the sibling controls.
observations.evidence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:110`; pr-body "This PR does not, so a programmatic change clears a server error on a Switch but not on an Input."

observations.fact: The mount effect no longer clears `filled` for an empty controlled value, so a control remounted with `value=""` under a persisting, already-filled `Field.Root` keeps `data-filled` where the merge-base cleared it; later value changes still update it through `useValueChanged`.

requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-115 syncs dirty, filled, form errors, and validation from `serializedValue`; test "syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically" passes at head.

requirements.source: pr-body/"The control now registers the serialized value, so the baseline and the comparison agree."
requirements.evidence: Compliance met: FieldControl.tsx:86,93 registers `String(value)`; useFieldControlRegistration.ts:97 captures it as `initialValue`; test "clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value" passes. Compatibility unresolved (linked question field-validity/serialized-value-type): `Field.Validity.State.initialValue`/`value` and the submit-time `validate` argument become strings for non-string controlled values; docs type both `unknown`, `value` was already the DOM string after any keystroke at base, no in-repo consumer conflicts, no release decision recorded.

No `processedValueRef` exists (observation).

requirements.source: pr-body/"`details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:153 guards `clearErrors` and `validation.change` with `!details.isCanceled`; test "does not validate when the change is canceled" passes. For an uncontrolled control dirty/filled still track the already-changed DOM value, matching the existing `defaultPrevented` path; for a controlled control nothing internal runs on the DOM event.
